title: A fasta with CRLF line endings fails to parse
body:
`FastaParser::parse` in `nail/src/io/fasta.rs` splits a record at its first `\n` into the header and the sequence, then drops every `\n` from the sequence. It keeps `\r`. In a fasta with Windows line endings every sequence line ends in `\r`. `UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO` has no entry for byte 13, so the parse fails with `byte: "13" is not in the compressed amino acid alphabet` and nail stops. nail does not produce wrong output from such a file.

This session found it by reading the code. Nobody has run nail on a CRLF file to confirm it.

The parser moves to `Sequence::from_fasta` in libnail under nail-167dd7, so a fix belongs there. The p7hmm parser also splits lines at `\n`, and this session did not check how it treats `\r`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text:
Diagnosis at `7db351a`, confirmed by running nail. With every line of `fixtures/target.fa` ending in CRLF, `nail search` against `fixtures/query.hmm`, with the fixture seeds converted to positions, stops with "no seq ... byte: \"13\" is not in the compressed amino acid alphabet". The parser is `Sequence::from_fasta` in `libnail/src/structs/sequence.rs`. It splits the header at the first `\n`, filters only `\n` from the sequence lines, and maps every other byte through `UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO`, which has no entry for 13. On a CRLF header with no description, the name would also keep its `\r`.

A CRLF `query.hmm` runs, and its 408 hits match the LF run exactly once sorted. `Profile::from_p7hmm` trims header lines and reads model lines with `split_whitespace`, both of which drop `\r`.

Easel, in `~/hmmer-3.4/easel/esl_sqio_ascii.c`, sets `inmap['\r'] = eslDSQ_IGNORED` with the comment "DOS eol compatibility". It ends the description at `\n` or `\r`, and ends the name at any whitespace (`isspace`).
